note: Repo-managed candidate registry for scripts/ftn-scout-candidate-tracker.mjs -- not a database. Full research findings, verification sources and decision rationale for each candidate live in SCOUT-INTELLIGENCE-LEDGER.md; this file carries only the fields the tracker needs to diff a candidate week over week (license, decision, a short summary, security notes, status). None of the candidates below are installed, deployed, or given any FTN credential -- this is a research record, exactly like js/ibis-provider-registry.js entries with enabled:false.

candidates.name: Hermes Agent
candidates.summary: Self-hostable, multi-LLM-provider agent runtime with skills/memory/cron/multi-platform messaging. Real candidate for an orchestration layer underneath ibis -- not a replacement for it. Bring-your-own-keys; no mandatory cloud account.
candidates.securityNotes: No production credentials required to evaluate. Real trial deployment needs a compute host (VPS/container) FTN has not provisioned -- a small but real new recurring cost requiring founder sign-off before anything beyond local/dev experimentation. Must never receive Supabase service-role, Cloudflare, or founder Gmail credentials; must never be exposed as a public product or renamed to imply it is ibis.

candidates.name: Agent Reach
candidates.summary: Source-access adapter giving an agent read-only research access to Twitter/X, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili and others. YouTube and public GitHub need no login; X, Reddit, XiaoHongShu, Facebook/Instagram require cookie-based or logged-in sessions. Read-only -- no publishing/account-action capability found in the project itself.
candidates.securityNotes: The project's own README warns of platform account-restriction risk from cookie login and recommends disposable, non-primary accounts -- exactly the risk this pass's security addendum flags. Selective adoption means: the no-login platforms (YouTube, public GitHub, Bilibili) are safe to sandbox now; the cookie-gated platforms (X, Reddit, XHS, Facebook/Instagram) are OUT OF SCOPE unless a separately-approved, non-founder, disposable account is provisioned -- never founder personal cookies or accounts.

candidates.name: last30days
candidates.summary: A coding-agent skill (not a standalone agent) that researches a topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, GitHub, arXiv and more from the last 30 days, scored by real engagement and synthesized into one cited brief. Reddit/HN/GitHub/arXiv need no credentials; X and several video/social platforms need either cookies or a paid key (ScrapeCreators, 10,000 free calls then pay-as-you-go).
candidates.securityNotes: Executes real subprocesses (yt-dlp, arxiv-cli, techmeme-cli) and extracts browser cookies from installed browsers for some paid-tier platforms -- both require the least-privilege sandbox boundary from this pass's security addendum (allowlisted subprocesses/paths, no unrestricted filesystem access). Initial experimentation should use only the free, no-cookie data paths (Reddit, HN, GitHub, arXiv, web search).

candidates.name: Graphiti
candidates.summary: Temporal knowledge graph framework for AI-agent memory (Zep's open-source core). Tracks how facts change over time with real provenance to source data -- the real architecture pattern for a future ibis institutional-memory layer.
candidates.securityNotes: Requires a graph database server (Neo4j, FalkorDB or Amazon Neptune) plus an LLM API key -- genuinely new backend infrastructure this repo (static site + Supabase Edge Functions, no database server) does not have. No safe way to "experiment" with it without first provisioning a graph database, which is out of scope for this pass -- resolved to PREPARE_NOW (schema/design thinking only) rather than EXPERIMENT, and flagged as a real Cloudflare/infrastructure-decision STOP CONDITION if pursued further.

candidates.name: Shandu
candidates.summary: Python deep-research agent: iterative research loops, per-source credibility scoring (source_class + credibility_score), and citation-backed synthesis that explicitly downgrades claims supported only by weak sources. The credibility/confidence-separation pattern this pass's own js/ftn-source-provenance.js borrows and reimplements natively in JS -- Shandu itself (Python, LiteLLM, pipx-installed) is not run or installed.
candidates.securityNotes: No installation planned -- this decision is architecture-borrowing only, not a code dependency. If ever run directly, it needs an LLM API key and executes real web scraping (trafilatura/readability/BS4, no headless browser) -- would need the same allowlisting discipline as last30days.

candidates.name: Webwright
candidates.summary: Microsoft Research browser agent that writes and runs real Playwright scripts instead of predicting clicks. Secondary-sweep finding: a genuinely different capability from the 5 primary candidates (code-generating browser automation), potentially relevant to a future Walkthrough rendering pipeline -- but that pipeline is explicitly out of scope for this pass.
candidates.securityNotes: Not evaluated in security depth this pass -- flagged as WATCH, not evaluated for adoption. Executes generated Playwright/Bash; would need the same sandboxing discipline as any code-executing agent before real use.

candidates.name: Crawl4AI
candidates.summary: Mature, popular (#1 trending at time of this research) LLM-ready web crawler turning arbitrary pages into clean Markdown for RAG/agents. Secondary-sweep finding: a more general-purpose, cookie-free alternative to Agent Reach specifically for public, non-authenticated web content -- does not cover the login-gated platforms Agent Reach targets.
candidates.securityNotes: Not evaluated in security depth this pass. Multi-browser crawling (Chromium/Firefox/WebKit) implies the same subprocess/network allowlisting discipline as any browser-automation tool before real use.

candidates.name: nanobot (HKUDS)
candidates.summary: Ultra-lightweight self-hosted Python agent framework (WebUI, MCP, multi-agent workflows). Secondary-sweep finding: real project, but capability materially overlaps Hermes Agent's role (agent runtime/orchestration) without a clearly distinct advantage found this pass -- recorded for reference, not separately pursued, to avoid evaluating two candidates for the same architectural slot.
candidates.securityNotes: License not independently verified this pass (distinct from the similarly-named github.com/nanobot-ai/nanobot Go MCP host, which is a different project) -- do not treat as license-cleared until verified directly.

candidates.name: Radar Intelligence
candidates.summary: No confident, specific public repository matching this name was located this pass. Search results returned only generically-named, unrelated "radar"-themed AI-agent projects (an LLMOps radar, an agentic-security scanner) with no clear connection to the named candidate.

candidates.name: Prismis
candidates.summary: No confident, specific public repository matching this exact name was located this pass. A similarly-named but distinct project ("prism-ai-deep-research", a different author/name) surfaced and was deliberately not treated as a match -- recording an unverified guess as if it were the intended candidate would misattribute findings to the wrong project.

candidates.name: Harken
candidates.summary: No public repository or project matching this name in a research/intelligence-agent context was located this pass.

candidates.name: Pith
candidates.summary: No confident match in a research/intelligence-agent context. The only "Pith" project found (mlc-ai/pith-train) is a Mixture-of-Experts model TRAINING system, an unrelated domain -- not recorded as a match to avoid misattributing an ML-training tool as a research/reconnaissance candidate.
